arXiv:1812.08509 §3.4 Theorem 1 and Gaussian kernel example
correctness.rationale: Gaussian strict positive definiteness ensures invertibility for finite positive lambda. Reflection fixes the weight vector and gives the positive-definite even block with determinant Delta>0 and the two stated Cramer numerators. Independent integration of the first three Taylor terms reproduces Delta=8(b²-a²)² lambda²+O(lambda³) and the stated numerator coefficients, so both limiting weights are positive when a²<1/3<b². An independent rational certificate uses signed Lagrange remainders: orders 23 and 24 enclose exp(-z) for z>=0 and can therefore also enclose each translated Gaussian mass by termwise integration. Outward rounded exact intervals for outer numerator, inner numerator and Delta at lambda=2 are respectively [-0.021574,-0.021572], [0.132727,0.132729] and [0.243788,0.243789]. For fixed interior nodes, sqrt(lambda)F tends to sqrt(pi)/2 and the even block tends to identity, giving eventual positivity. Continuity supplies two distinct outer-weight zeros and an open neighborhood of radii with the same sign-return pattern. Exactly two positive weights at lambda=2 attain the known general two-of-four lower bound; there is no need for a full count of outer-weight zeros or for the inner weights to stay positive at every shape.
residual_risks: The signs are for finite positive lambda. The robust perturbations are of the two radii within the symmetric family. The proof gives at least two outer-weight zeros, not exactly two.

evidence: The total positivity theorem gives at least floor((n+1)/2) positive weights, and variance-local optimality supplies a separate all-positive condition. The flat-Gaussian theorem gives convergence to polynomial cubature weights. Oettershagen compares optimized designs and errors across shapes.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The sharp lower bound is known as a bound, and the flat limit is covered. The fixed nodes are not assumed locally optimal. None of the compared general statements supplies an attaining fixed symmetric design at finite shape that also exhibits the two strict positive regimes.

originality.rationale: The verified addition is a fixed four-site Gaussian design on a uniform interval attaining exactly two positive weights at an intermediate shape and recovering strict positivity at both shape extremes, robustly in the radii. Neither negative weights in general, the lower bound, nor convergence to polynomial weights in the flat limit is new.
residual_risks: Comparison is bounded; a fixed-site sign sweep may exist outside the inspected sections or in other examples. No chronological priority is inferred from the same-day three-node record.

value.rationale: A fixed-node rule may be positive in both standard asymptotic regimes yet fail to be a positive functional at a practical intermediate scale. The strictly negative outer pair shows that the general half-positive bound is sharp even in a simple symmetric Gaussian design; the certificate and open-neighborhood result exclude a floating-point artifact or a single fine-tuned geometry.
residual_risks: No accuracy loss estimate, exact crossing count, or claim of optimal nodes is inferred from signs alone.
